cognitive_contract.label: Justify / formal deductive proof (National/International Olympiad)
cognitive_contract.decisive_act: Formulate and discriminate unassailable deductive justifications, probabilistic existence arguments, sharpness equality conditions, and infinite descent contradiction proofs without intermediate scaffolding.
cognitive_contract.band_protected_work: Require learner to establish the complete deductive necessity across probabilistic permutation indicators, Cauchy reverse algebraic substitutions, or iterated Pythagorean parameterizations.
cognitive_contract.support_posture: Activate the foundational framework (random variables, reverse algebraic expansions, or modular parity) without completing the contradiction or equality proof.

slots.X: proving the Caro-Wei lower bound on graph independence numbers via random vertex permutations and linearity of expectation
slots.Y: simple graph G = (V, E) with vertex degrees d(v)
slots.Z: random permutation ordering: vertex v is chosen if it precedes all neighbors in N(v); probability is 1/(d(v)+1); linearity of expectation guarantees existence of independent set of size at least sum 1/(d(v)+1)
slots.W: Assigning each vertex a uniform random permutation of {1, ..., n} and selecting vertices that precede all their neighbors produces an independent set whose expected size by linearity of expectation is sum 1/(d(v)+1), guaranteeing an independent set of at least that size.
slots.wrong_idea: claiming a naive greedy vertex-deletion heuristic achieves the bound without tie-breaking, or using independent coin-flips which yields the weaker Turan bound
slots.replacement_rule: use uniform random permutation of V; the indicator that v precedes N(v) has expectation 1/(d(v)+1); linearity of expectation proves existence
slots.visual_job: render small sample graph with vertices ordered by random permutation, highlighting the selected independent set; avoid unmounted SVGs
slots.check_job: independent verification: test on complete graph K_n where d(v) = n-1: sum 1/((n-1)+1) = sum 1/n = 1 = alpha(K_n); test on empty graph E_n where d(v) = 0: sum 1/1 = n = alpha(E_n). Bounds are sharp.

core2_custody.stem_requirement: Exact formulation of an international Olympiad formal justification or proof discrimination demand
core2_custody.hint_ladder_requirement: H1 activates the foundational proof framework; H2 establishes intermediate contradiction step; preserves W
core2_custody.solution_requirement: Locked pre-commit; complete formal step-by-step deductive derivation evaluating W
core2_custody.distractor_requirement: Every distractor explained with specific student proof error, circularity, or pseudo-justification

core1a_declarative.anti_leak_rule: Strict prohibition on leaking Core 2 exact parameters or textual answer in Core 1A text

core1b_reconstruction.rule: Targeted active recall eliciting the core proof invariant before problem execution

core2a_navigation.rule: Explicit question-specific data-core-unit-id navigation hook required in DOM representation

precommit_dom_privacy.rule: Neutral buttons, no data-correct / is_correct attributes, locked details container with inert and hidden
